article.name: AgentDatabase

article.summary: AgentDatabase is a multi-project agent-data repository whose OpenAIDatabase subsystem stores structured personal memories as canonical, sharded JSONL with governed mutations and temporal retrieval. Selected source code was inspected at the verified main head; no system benchmark was run.

who_what.text: The root repository contains multiple agent-data projects. Its README identifies OpenAIDatabase as the local-first conversation and memory runtime, alongside a retired MemoryAtlas app and a CodexSkills mirror. The reviewed memory functionality is the Python CLI and structured personal database under OpenAIDatabase.

architecture.text: Code observation: canonical memory is a manifest and deterministically planned records-NNNN.jsonl shards under data/memory/records. The CLI validates the record set and its writer stages, fsyncs, installs, then reloads and validates the complete canonical dataset. Generated agent-memory views are built separately.

The V2 record schema includes record identity and statement fields, status, typed scope, source reference and observed time, optional evidence hash, valid and recorded time, confidence and importance, verification state/references, tags and aliases, sensitivity, conflict/supersession, and content hash. The architecture document identifies candidate, active, disputed, and retired records in the canonical store.

behavior.text: Write: mutation envelopes carry operation, content-derived idempotency key, base commit, actor, source, authorization, target scope, payload, valid time, sensitivity, and reason. Supported operation types are add, update, retire, and dispute. Policy rejects raw_import and model_inference as canonical persistence sources.

Update: the implementation retires the active target, appends a transition, links the old record to a successor, and appends the successor record. Retirement and dispute also append recorded-time transitions. No physical delete operation is present in the inspected operation set.

Deletion: forgetting policy defines retirement as retrieval exclusion rather than history deletion; the schema also forbids canonical business-record rewrite in task. This source review found no canonical physical-delete operation.

Retrieval: query accepts filters by ID, key, kind, scope, tags, keyword, valid-time as-of, recorded-time as-of, inactive inclusion, and bounded result limit. Current answer eligibility is active and effective only; inactive records can be shown for audit, while the decision layer can return UNKNOWN with a reason and missing conditions.

Scope: schema scope types are global, project, task, and conversation. Query scope is optional, and the local CLI does not authenticate a caller; mutation policy restricts repository-evidence writes to project/task scopes. This establishes filtering and admission rules, not authenticated tenant isolation.

Provenance: records include source type/reference/observed time and evidence hash, plus verification state, method, references, verified time, and rationale. Repository-evidence writes require a hash under policy. These structures do not by themselves establish that every stored claim is supported by its source.

metrics.evidence: No AgentDatabase answerable or unanswerable probes were run.
Source implements update as retirement plus successor and exposes temporal query axes; no post-correction probes were run.
No deletion probes were run; inspected canonical operations include retirement but no physical delete.
No cross-scope probes were run; optional query filters do not establish an authorization boundary.

metrics.domain: Evidence support precision and citation coverage
metrics.evidence: The schema contains source and verification references, but no generated claims and citations were adjudicated.
The source contains configured request/cache budgets and a local benchmark command; this review collected no timings.
No workload token, charge, or attributable storage measurements were collected.

Configured retrieval limits include at most two indexed-fact content fetches, zero recursive full-tree scans, three attempts, and a 120-second retry budget. The CLI exposes JSON result status and query scan/filter/exclusion counts. These are source-level contracts, not measured results.

limits.text: This is a bounded review of selected README, architecture, schema, policy, and Python source files at the pinned main head. It does not establish runtime correctness, answer quality, actual latency/cost/storage, or production reliability.

Scope filters and mutation admission constraints are visible in source, but no authenticated cross-principal or cross-tenant isolation tests were run. Retirement excludes a record from current answers but does not erase canonical history.

The repository README says the MemoryAtlas application has been retired; this article assesses OpenAIDatabase memory code and does not treat the retained app code as an active memory service. The checked official documentation did not publish a contact email.

benchmark.note: No AgentDatabase system or benchmark workload was executed. Source observations, configured budgets, metric definitions, and the synthetic fixture are not benchmark results.
